posts.title: 5 Things to Consider Before Hiring a Car in Zambia
posts.content:
Whether you're a business traveller, a tourist, or a local company needing additional fleet capacity, hiring a car in Zambia can be a smart move. But not all car hire services are created equal. Here are five critical factors to consider.

1. Insurance Coverage. Always verify the comprehensive insurance policy covers third-party liability, collision damage, and theft. Ask for the policy documentation before signing.

2. Mileage Limits. Some providers cap daily mileage. For longer trips between Lusaka, Kabwe, and the Copperbelt, an unlimited-mileage option is essential.

3. Driver Requirements. Confirm the minimum age, licence requirements, and whether a Zambian driving permit is needed for foreign visitors.

4. Vehicle Condition. Check the vehicle's service history, tyre condition, and whether the fleet is regularly maintained. At Nexpark, every vehicle is meticulously inspected before each rental.

5. Roadside Assistance. A 24/7 roadside assistance line is non-negotiable, especially for trips outside major cities. Nexpark offers 24/7 support on every rental.

To book a vehicle with Nexpark Enterprises, contact us at +260 955 937 272.

posts.title: How to Choose the Right Construction Partner in Zambia
posts.content:
Construction is one of the largest investments any business or family will make. Choosing the right construction partner can mean the difference between a project delivered on time and on budget — and a costly, stressful experience. Here are six questions to ask before signing any contract.

1. Are they registered? Verify the contractor's PACRA registration and, for engineering projects, their Engineering Registration Board (EngRB) classification.

2. Can they show similar completed projects? Ask for references and site visits. A track record speaks louder than any pitch.

3. Do they have in-house capabilities? Companies with integrated design, fabrication, electrical, and plumbing teams reduce subcontractor risk and improve turnaround times.

4. What is their safety record? Ask about PPE compliance, worker insurance, and site safety protocols.

5. How do they handle variations and delays? Get written processes for change orders, timeline adjustments, and payment milestones.

6. Are they financially stable? Request proof of tax clearance, NAPSA compliance, and Workers' Compensation registration.

Nexpark Enterprises is registered with PACRA, ZRA, NAPSA, and the Engineering Registration Board (Civil Engineering, Class C2). We deliver residential and commercial projects across Central Province and Lusaka.

posts.title: Sustainable Farming: How Nexpark Delivers Farm-Fresh Food in Lusaka

posts.title: Bulk Procurement: 7 Reasons to Choose a Local Zambian Supplier
posts.content:
When your organisation needs to procure goods in bulk — whether office stationery, PPE, medical supplies, or building materials — choosing a local Zambian supplier offers significant advantages over international sourcing.

1. Faster Delivery. No customs clearance, no port delays. Local suppliers deliver in days, not weeks.

2. Lower Total Cost. Reduced shipping, duties, and currency risk often outweigh any unit price difference.

3. Easier Returns. Defective or incorrect items can be exchanged quickly and without international shipping headaches.

4. Local Support. Same-timezone communication, on-site visits, and faster issue resolution.

5. Compliance. Local suppliers are registered with ZRA, ZPPA, NAPSA, and PACRA — providing documentation your procurement department needs.

6. Contribution to Local Economy. Every kwacha spent locally supports Zambian jobs and communities.

7. Customisation. Need branded uniforms or specific packaging? Local suppliers can adapt quickly.

Nexpark Enterprises Limited is a ZPPA-registered local supplier covering 13 procurement categories.

posts.title: PPE Essentials: What Every Zambian Worksite Needs in 2025
posts.content:
Workplace safety is non-negotiable. Whether you run a construction site, a factory, a mine, or a warehouse, having the right Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) protects your team and keeps your operations compliant with Zambian safety regulations.

Essential PPE for 2025:

Head Protection: Hard hats (Class A, B, or C depending on hazard). Replace any helmet that has sustained impact or shows cracks.

Eye & Face Protection: Safety glasses, goggles, and full-face shields. Required for welding, grinding, chemical handling, and woodworking.

Hearing Protection: Earplugs or earmuffs for environments above 85 dB.

Respiratory Protection: N95 masks, half-face respirators, or full-face respirators depending on airborne hazards.

Hand Protection: Cut-resistant, chemical-resistant, and thermal gloves matched to the specific task.

Foot Protection: Steel-toe or composite-toe safety boots. Ensure proper fit and slip resistance.

High-Visibility Clothing: Reflective vests, jackets, and trousers for any site with moving vehicles or low-light conditions.

Nexpark Enterprises supplies a complete range of certified PPE — including custom-branded uniforms and workwear. Bulk orders welcome.
